description.narrative: The DISC Programme aims to support the efforts of the government of Uganda to promote digitalisation, innovation and smart cities to accelerate Uganda’s structural transformation

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

Output 1: By 2025 Uganda’s enabling environment is strengthened and supporting accelerated digital transformation, growth of a strong and integrated innovation and start-up ecosystem, and development of accountable, smart and sustainable cities. Output Indicator 1.1: # of policy and legal frameworks developed at national and subnational levels creating equal opportunities, pro-poor growth and sustainable development. Results for target 1.1 ( under output indicator 1.1): Four (4) Strategies out of three (3) and Policy drafted. - Long-term Gender sensitive Digital Roadmap - Big Data Utilization Strategy - E-commerce strategy and Policy - Start Ecosystem Strategy
Indicator 1.2: # of target institutions with functional e-governance systems to promote efficiency and accountability. Result for target 1.2: Zero (0).
Indicator 1.3: # of targeted non-state institutions with strengthened capacities for advocacy and engagement in the review and reform of legislation and policies for national and subnational governance and development. Result for target 1.3: One (1) out of two (2) Supported Centenary Technology Services to design the digital transformation roadmap and the bigdata utilization strategy.
Indicator 1.4: An inclusive functional strategic platform for government engagement with private sector on digital policy review, learning and policy advocacy in place. Result for target 1.4 (Indicator 1.4): A beta version of E-learning platform designed. The DISC Programme also worked with Ministry of Trade to design an e-learning platform for self-paced learning for MSMEs. A beta version of this platform can be accessed on this link https://digitalskillsforsme.com.
Indicator 1.5: # of innovative, locally appropriate sustainable development initiatives developed and scaled up, targeting underserved communities/groups and women. Results for target 1.5: One (1) out of four (4) Locally innovative Solution for Forests Monitoring designed. The Natural Resources Information System (NARIS) was designed with the Accelerator Lab and handed over to the Nature, Climate, Energy and Resilience (NCER) team for Scaling up to add wetlands.
Indicator 1.6: # of diagnostics (special studies, analytics) conducted to inform policy options. Result for target 1.6: Four (4) diagnostics/Assessments done to inform the development of the below Policies/Strategies. - Long-term Gender sensitive Digital Roadmap - Big Data Utilization Strategy - E-commerce strategy and Policy - Start Ecosystem Strategy
Indicator 1.7: # of public-private partnerships to improve the enabling framework for economic diversification and green growth (IRRF 2.1.1.2) Result under target 1.7: Three (3) partnerships were established and three (3) Innovation Hubs equipped with machinery for prototyping for instance, a Multi- disciplinary Makerere University Innovation Pod, Ministry of ICT National ICT Innovation Hub and Kampala Capital City (KCCA) Innovation Hub have been equipped with machinery for prototyping to enable economic diversification and green growth.
Output 2: By 2025 the level of literacy and ICT skilling in Uganda is inclusively raised to significantly impact the use of digital tools to access online government and private sector service and is driving digital content development and the growth of the ICT start-up ecosystem. Indicator 2.1: # of digital platforms created for citizen participation and as channels for mass digital literacy & use. Result for target 2.1: One (1) beta version of E-learning platform designed. The DISC Programme also worked with Ministry of Trade to design an e-learning platform for self-paced learning for MSMEs. A beta version of this platform can be accessed on this link https://digitalskillsforsme.com.
Indicator 2.2: A functional Digital Skills Acceleration Programme in place to support e-education in pilot primary and secondary schools. Result for target 2.2: Under the Long-term Gender Sensitive Digital Roadmap, the DISC Programme Initiated the National Digital Skills literacy Acceleration Programme pilot in Primary and Secondary schools.
Indicator 2.3: # of beneficiaries of UNDP supported Digital Acceleration initiatives disaggregated by sex Result for target 2.3: Zero (0).
Indicator 2.4: # of accredited institutions established to offer certified skilling, entrepreneurship, and incubation development. Results for target 2.4: Seventy eight (78) registered Startup Ecosystem mapped. Designed a platform which brings together the startup ecosystem who are mainly Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), so far mapped 78 start-up, 11 Accelerators and 2 Coworking Spaces. Platform can be accessed on this link https://uganda.startupblink.com/.
Output 3: By 2025, digitalization of critical services for leading production, social and governance sectors is gender responsive and equitably accelerated to enhance agri-business, tourism, trade, digital economy, creative industries, health, and public sector effectiveness. Indicator 3.1: # of innovative, locally appropriate sustainable development initiatives developed and scaled up, targeting underserved communities/groups and women. Result for target 3.1: One (1) out of ten (10) Locally innovative Solution for Forests Monitoring designed. The Natural Resources Information System (NARIS) was designed with the Accelerator Lab and handed over to the NCER team for Scaling up to add wetlands.
Indicator 3.2: # of new functional partnerships between government, academia, development partners and civil society developed to promote digital literacy and skilling. Result for target 3.2: Functional partnership have been established with three government institutions for instance; a multi- disciplinary Makerere University Innovation Pod, Ministry of ICT National ICT Innovation Hub and Kampala Capital City (KCCA) Innovation Hub have been equipped with machinery for prototyping to enable economic diversification and green growth. Due to these partnerships the capacity of over 500 end-users has been strengthened in digital skills, including Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) and , District Local Governments (DLGs). Government staff got skills in the digital Integration of Government Systems, Digital Authentication and Electronic Signatures, E-Payment Gateway, UMCS.
Indicator 3.3: Amount of financial resources mobilised to implement public-private and civil society partnerships for the development of digital solutions. Result for target 3.3: Mobilised a total of USD 911,322 from Trac 2, Timbaktoo Project and CDO DPGA.
Indicators 3.4: # of target institutions (National and sub-national level) with improved capacities to plan, budget, manage and monitor basic services (IRRF 1.2.1.1) Result for target 3.4: The capacity of over 500 end-users was strengthened in digital skills, including Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) and , District Local Governments (DLGs). Government staff got skills in the digital Integration of Government Systems, Digital Authentication and Electronic Signatures, E-Payment Gateway, UMCS. The trained institution now have the capacity to digitally plan, budget, manage and monitor their services.
